expectations.text: Response calls getCanvasState with a wide focusArea (covering a large coordinate range such as x: -5000, y: -5000, w: 20000, h: 20000) as the first step before moving any frames.
expectations.evidence: Response shows exact call: `getCanvasState({ focusArea: { x: -5000, y: -5000, w: 20000, h: 20000 } })` and explains 'Use a wide focusArea (the -5000 to +20000 range shown above) because scattered frames may have drifted far from the origin'.

expectations.text: Response recommends writing a coordinate table — computing each frame's x and y before touching the canvas — to turn reorganisation into a single applyCanvasActions batch.
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'Coordinate table — Compute the final x and y for every frame and label on paper or in a spreadsheet before touching the canvas. Then — and only then — batch all moves into a single applyCanvasActions call.'

expectations.text: Response warns to abort and investigate if an expected shape ID is missing from the getCanvasState result before issuing move commands.
expectations.evidence: Response quotes the skill directly: '"Abort and investigate if an expected shape ID is missing before issuing any move commands."'

expectations.text: Response specifies using recommended gutter values: 80 px sibling gutter (between frames in the same zone) and 160 px zone gutter (between zones).
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'Recommended defaults: 80 px sibling gutter (between frames in the same zone), 160 px zone gutter (between zones).'
